prologue.motivation: Dashboards would break during deploys, so people had to keep refreshing until things came back.
prologue.outcome: Dashboards stay up during deploys now.

graph LR
  A[Dashboard] --> B[ApiClient]

keyChanges.summary: API calls now survive a deploy blip
keyChanges.description: Transient 503s are retried with backoff instead of surfacing as errors.

keyChanges.summary: The backoff ceiling is covered by tests
keyChanges.description: The maximum delay remains bounded even after many retry attempts.

focusAreas.title: Backoff helper
focusAreas.description: First use of a shared backoff utility — confirm the base delay and cap suit our traffic.

focusAreas.title: Retry budget
focusAreas.description: Verify max retries won't pile up request load during a sustained outage.

complexity.reasoning: New shared utility plus a behavioural change in the API client.

chapters.title: Add a reusable backoff helper
chapters.summary:
Introduces `backoff()` — a small utility that computes exponential delays with a ceiling.

Later chapters build on this to retry failed requests without hammering the backend.

keyChanges.content: Is a 100ms base with a 5s cap the right shape for our request volume, or should the cap be lower?

chapters.title: Retry transient failures in the API client
chapters.summary:
Now that `backoff()` exists, the API client retries 503s instead of throwing.

This is the change that actually keeps dashboards alive through a deploy.

keyChanges.content: Should retries be capped per-request, or share a global budget so an outage can't multiply load?

chapters.title: Cover the backoff ceiling
chapters.summary: Pins the maximum delay with a direct test, so an extreme retry count cannot silently grow the wait beyond five seconds.
